NerfTree is a two-level sparse voxel structure designed to accelerate Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) by localizing geometry and radiance estimation to surface-adjacent regions, thereby skipping empty space [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes NerfTree as a 'two-level octree' (which is a two-level sparse voxel structure) composed of a 'coarse density voxel volume' and 'fine sparse voxel grids'. It states that the coarse volume is used to 'localize the object's surface' and the fine grids are used to 'refine geometry and radiance estimation in surface-adjacent regions'. The source also mentions that this approach accelerates NeRF by focusing on these regions, effectively skipping empty space (implied by the sparse nature and the reduction in training time). All specific facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
